pr_title: Bluetooth: SMP: Fix setting key distribution bits for no-bonding
pr_body:
9.4.2 section, Part C, Vol 3 of the Bluetooth Core specification v5.3 states the following in the case that the device is in non-bondable mode:

If Security Manager pairing is supported, the Host shall set the Bonding_Flags to ‘No Bonding’ as defined in [Vol 3] Part H, Section 3.5.1 and bonding information shall not be exchanged or stored.

Fixes #54104

Signed-off-by: Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com>
pr_comments: Note: this is only build tested. I don't have time to runtime test it, so someone needs to do that before this can be merged.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: Bonding information distribution in the non-bondable mode
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Zephyr Bluetooth Host (SMP module) seems to violate the Bluetooth specification in the following pairing corner case. With the Bonding Flag (BF) cleared in the Pairing Response, the stack should also set the key distribution flags to zero for the key distribution initiator and the responder. In this case, the specification requires no bonding information distribution (IRK, Identity Address, LTK, etc.).

This requirement is based on the 9.4.2 section, Part C, Vol 3 of the Bluetooth Core specification v5.3:

> 
> 9.4.2 Non-bondable mode
>  
> 9.4.2.1 Description
> A device in the non-bondable mode does not allow a bond to be created with a peer device.
>  
> 9.4.2.2 Conditions
> If a device does not support pairing as defined in the Security Manager section then it is considered to be in non-bondable mode. **If Security Manager pairing is supported, the Host shall set the Bonding_Flags to ‘No Bonding’ as defined in [Vol 3] Part H, Section 3.5.1 and bonding information shall not be exchanged or stored.**

**To Reproduce**
Set the non-bondable mode for the Bluetooth Peripheral device using the following configuration ```CONFIG_BT_BONDABLE=n``` and pair with the Central device (e.g. Android device) that requests bonding in the Pairing Request. Observe in the sniffer trace or HCI logs that bonding information is exchanged between devices.

**Expected behavior**
Bonding information shall not be exchanged in the non-bondable mode.
comments:
I'm quite sure the Zephyr implementation has been like this from the very beginning (i.e. for many years), and AFAIK there hasn't been any issue with interoperability or passing qualification tests. Is there some new test case that fails because of this? To be clear, we don't ignore the bonding flag, but the effect of it is limited to what we do with the keys after the pairing procedure, i.e. if we store the keys for later connections or not.

@sjanc @Vudentz @carlescufi any thoughts on this?

For me it looks like we violating the spec requirement (shall). The fact that there is currently no conformance tests for this specific requirement does not mean they will not appear later. From IOP perspective I think it would be better to clear key distribution flags in that case, preventing peer from taking ambiguous decision to accept / distribute keys in Non-bondable mode.

@seko-nordic does it make any difference if we're doing Secure Connections pairing or legacy LE pairing? For SC, some of the flags are about generation, not distribution, which wouldn't violate the word of the spec.

@jhedberg It should not make any difference. If you are thinking about LTK in LESC, it is always generated and the spec explicitly prohibit to distribute it, see
3.6.1 Key distribution and generation
BLUETOOTH CORE SPECIFICATION Version 5.3 | Vol 3, Part H page 1611
In LE Secure Connections pairing, when SMP is running on the LE
transport, then the EncKey field shall be ignored. EDIV and Rand shall be
set to zero and shall not be distributed.

I've submitted PR #54429 as an attempt to fix this, but I don't have the possibility of running any actual tests with this change, so someone else needs to test it. The effect of that PR should be that we set both initiator and responder distribution bits to zero whenever either side has indicated that it does not intend to bond.

review_comments:
I'm a little confused about this. 

The spec does state, as you write in the commit message, that 
> bonding information shall not be exchanged or stored

"Bonding information" is then defined as 
> The security and identity information as defined in [Vol 3] Part H, Section 2.4.1 is also known as the bonding information

"Security information" is then defined as 
> security information (LTK, EDIV, and Rand)

But in 5.3, vol 3, Part H, 2.4.4.2 Encryption setup using LTK it also states
> The Central must have the security information (LTK, EDIV, and Rand) distributed by the Peripheral in LE legacy pairing or the LTK generated in LE Secure Connections to setup an encrypted session.

So if bonding is not supported, then we shall not exchange the security information, but the spec also states that the security information shall be exchanged to encrypt the link (as I read it anyhow). Doesn't this (wrongly) imply that if you don't support bonding, you cannot encrypt the link? :s 

Am I missing something?

One will not be able to re-encrypt the link after re-connection without re-pairing. That is exactly what is no-bonding about. It is still possible to encrypt the link in the end of pairing with STK in case of legacy pairing or LTK for LESC.
@jhedberg @alwa-nordic Any comments here? Am I misreading something, or is there a spec issue here?

> @jhedberg @alwa-nordic Any comments here? Am I misreading something, or is there a spec issue here?

I'm not sure I completely understand your concern. The situation is like @seko-nordic described in his earlier comment. You'll be able to encrypt, but just for the same connection that you run the SMP procedure over. That's how SMP with no-bonding is expected to behave.
I agree, but my concern is not with this PR, but the text in the specification. To me it seems that the definitions of bonding information and security information don't match up.
